network.tdh.spec.metadataDescription: The exact rule behind TDH: every input, formula and rounding step, in readable form.
network.tdh.spec.title: The TDH-v1 specification
network.tdh.spec.lede: TDH-v1 is the exact rule behind TDH, written so that independent programs produce identical results, to the last unit. It restates the formula 6529.io’s backend uses today; earlier boost schedules, listed under Historic boosts, differed. Where it departs from the backend, it removes a dependence on timing, database order, editable data or floating-point evaluation, and section 11 lists each departure with its measured effect.
network.tdh.spec.version: Rule version tdh-v1.0. Specification P26 as amended on 15 October 2026 (commit 0621ed4); a proposal, not yet adopted as a consensus rule. By the owner’s decisions, 6529.io computes it from the cutover, about 23 October 2026, and every validator computes it once validators run.
network.tdh.spec.mapDesc: Inputs (section 2) feed canonical events (3), which set the snapshot (4). Eligibility and rates (5) and identities (6) both feed holdings (7), which feed scores (8) and the day’s output (9). The parameters (10) feed sections 5 to 8.
network.tdh.spec.s1.title: 1. Scope and conventions
network.tdh.spec.s1.body: TDH-v1 defines, for one day, each wallet’s and each identity’s balance, whole days, base, boost and final TDH for every eligible token, and the network totals. Ranks, xTDH, REP and upload files are out of scope. All arithmetic is on integers or exact fractions. Where the old backend’s floating-point rounding matters, the rule names it exactly: B64 is the nearest binary64 number, and it only decides ties.
network.tdh.spec.s2.title: 2. Inputs
network.tdh.spec.s2.body: One day’s inputs are Ethereum’s canonical chain up to the snapshot block, every event of four contracts up to that block, the edition-floor state of a fifth contract read at that block, and the rule version’s parameter list. Prices, Meme Lab, received xTDH, REP and $6529 balances are not inputs.
network.tdh.spec.s2.tableCaption: Four event sources and one state read
network.tdh.spec.s2.delegationEvents: Register and revoke, direct and through a sub-delegate
network.tdh.spec.s2.manifoldEvents: getClaimForToken, read at the snapshot block
network.tdh.spec.s2.topicsCaption: Topic hashes, keccak-256 of each signature
network.tdh.spec.s3.title: 3. Canonical events
network.tdh.spec.s3.body: Every event is read exactly once, decoded strictly, and put in one order that everyone can reproduce: block, then transaction, then log, then position in a batch. A node that cannot show it has every event must not publish. A malformed event invalidates the day’s input rather than being skipped. Zero-amount and self transfers move nothing but are kept, because a zero-amount mint is how a card is created. Within one transaction, each token’s movements are first netted (section 7.1); the edition counts and the underflow test read the transfers before netting.
network.tdh.spec.s3.sinks: Mints, burns and sinks: a mint comes from the zero address and debits nobody. A transfer to the zero address or 0x…dead is a burn; the sinks receive records but are never debited. The FirstGM burn transaction is not credited to the zero address. Burns do not reduce edition sizes.
network.tdh.spec.s4.title: 4. Day, snapshot and whole days
network.tdh.spec.s4.body: Day N is the number of days since 1 January 1970; it closes at N × 86,400 seconds, 00:00 UTC. The snapshot block is the last block before that moment on the finalized chain, and the day has no result until the next block is finalized too. Ages are whole days measured to the snapshot block’s time. Example: the upload dated 2026-10-11 is day 20,737, boundary 1,791,676,800.
network.tdh.spec.s4.binds: The result binds (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash).
network.tdh.spec.s5.title: 5. Eligibility, editions, rates and seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.title: 5.1 Eligibility
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.body: Memes and Gradients count when their first mint, of any amount, is at least eligibility_min_age_s (86,400 s) before T. NextGen tokens count when minted at or before B. n_memes is the number of eligible Memes, a count.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.title: 5.2 Editions and floors
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.body: Burns do not reduce an edition. FirstGM’s edition is adjusted by −2,588. A Meme with fewer than 300 copies gets a floor, its claim’s totalMax capped at 310, and its edition is the larger of the floor and the minted count, because the final top-up airdrop takes it to 310, above The Memes’ 300-copy minimum (the Nakamoto Threshold). From 300 copies on there is no floor. A Meme with no claim has no floor. A Meme with an effective edition of 0 is eligible but has no rate, and holding a copy of it makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.title: 5.3 Rates
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.body: Meme i: RATE(H, E[i]). Gradient: RATE(H, G), at least 1.00, G = Gradients minted at or before B. NextGen token t: RATE(H, N_c), c = t div 10^10, N_c = tokens of collection c minted at or before B. With no eligible Meme, H = 0: Gradients get 1.00 and NextGen 0.
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.title: 5.4 Seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.body: Seasons come from a versioned list of first Meme ids: 1, 48, 87, 119, 152, 181, 213, 246, 279, 311, 343, 375, 407, 439, 477, 516, 556. A season is listed for a day when its first id is at most n_memes; the highest listed is current. Seasons 1 to 20 carry a 0.05 bonus; a season pays when it is not current and its bonus is positive. A new season must be added, as a new rule version, before its first card becomes eligible.
network.tdh.spec.s6.title: 6. Consolidation
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.title: 6.1 Events
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.body: Only delegation events with use case 999, for The Memes or the all-collections address 0x8888…8888, between two different wallets, count. Expiry, allTokens, token id and update events are ignored.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.title: 6.2 Pair state
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.body: Each unordered pair of wallets has at most one row. A registration in one direction is pending; the other direction confirms it. The collection does not partition the state.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.machineDesc: Three states: no row, pending from a to b, and confirmed. REGISTER(a, b) creates a pending row; REGISTER(b, a) on a pending row confirms it. REVOKE on a confirmed row returns it to pending in the other direction; REVOKE by the registering side of a pending row deletes it.
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.title: 6.3 Identities
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.body: Confirmed pairs, newest first, grow cliques of at most 3 wallets in which every pair is confirmed; a wallet joins at most one.
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.title: 6.4 and 6.5 Effective state and identity key
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.body: The grouping after all events up to B applies to the whole history of the day’s calculation. An identity’s key is its sorted lowercase addresses joined by “-”.
network.tdh.spec.s7.title: 7. Holdings
network.tdh.spec.s7.body: First an underflow test counts each wallet’s copies over the transfers before netting: a send of more than the wallet holds makes the input invalid. Then each transaction’s movements of each token are netted: every address’s net change, a sink’s included, with senders and receivers paired in ascending address order. The netted transfers are replayed in canonical order into a list of acquisition times per wallet and token; sends take from the end, and age carries only between wallets of one identity. Base per token is rounded per wallet; an identity’s base is the sum of its wallets’ bases, never recomputed from merged days. A wallet has a record when it holds an eligible token or belongs to a group; an identity has a record when one of its wallets does.
network.tdh.spec.s8.title: 8. Arithmetic and scores
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.title: 8.1 Rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.body: RATE equals half-up of 100n/d except at an exact half cent; with H = 3,941 that happens only for editions 8, 40, 56, 200, 280 and 1,400.
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.title: 8.2 Base
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.body: Multiply the rate in cents by the whole days and round half up to a whole TDH. This equals the old backend’s two-step rounding.
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.title: 8.3 Boost
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.body: A record holds a token when the token is eligible and the balance is positive, whatever the copies’ ages. ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 for n ≥ 33; the cent rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.title: 8.4 Final
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.body: FINAL is computed per token; a record’s final is the sum. Ties round down only for some boosts and some bases, the smallest being base 25 at 1.14.
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.title: 8.5 Totals
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.body: The total is the sum of identity finals; a second total excludes the zero and dead identities, which never enter any consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.title: 8.6 Daily rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.body: rate_e4 = beta × the sum of the rates of each copy with at least one whole day, in 10^-4 TDH a day; derived data.
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.title: 8.7 Range
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.body: A day is inside the tdh-v1.0 range when H, G, every N_c, every base × beta and the total are below 2^53, and every net movement of section 7.1’s netting is below 2^64 (vector 50). Outside it there is no result. Inside it, hardware binary64 and exact emulation agree.
network.tdh.spec.s9.title: 9. The day’s output
network.tdh.spec.s9.body: The header (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash), and per identity its key, wallets, boost and final, with per-token balance, raw, base and final. The per-token final is what card-set credit uses. Wallet records, daily rates and totals are derived.
network.tdh.spec.s10.title: 10. Parameters
network.tdh.spec.s10.body: Every number the rule uses is a parameter of the rule version. tdh-v1.0 is not frozen until launch: changes made before launch, such as D131’s transaction netting, stay tdh-v1.0. From launch on, a change to a rule or to a parameter is a new rule version with its own first cycle.
network.tdh.spec.s10.name: Name
network.tdh.spec.s10.hashNote: Recomputed with the Python reference; conformance vector 28 checks it.

network.tdh.spec.s11.title: 11. Where TDH-v1 differs from the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s11.body: Nineteen differences, each with what the old backend did, what TDH-v1 does, the measured effect and the decision. On the replayed cycle none changes a value: the only one that did, DEV-2, came from tokens sent out and back within one transaction, which D131’s netting removes.

network.tdh.spec.dev.4.old: Read whatever had been indexed by 00:01

network.tdh.spec.s12.title: 12. Issues found in the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s12.body: Fifteen issues the work on TDH-v1 found in the old backend’s calculation, and what TDH-v1 does about each. Most are removed; BUG-7’s carry over history and BUG-9 are kept by decision, and BUG-15 concerns upload files, which TDH-v1 does not define.
network.tdh.spec.bug.1.issue: The same-second ordering rule is inconsistent and can crash the run
network.tdh.spec.bug.2.issue: The order before sorting depends on which database query finishes first
network.tdh.spec.bug.3.issue: Indexing merges movements and drops their position
network.tdh.spec.bug.4.issue: Indexing follows the unfinalized chain and never revisits blocks
network.tdh.spec.bug.5.issue: The job does not wait for indexing to catch up
network.tdh.spec.bug.6.issue: The snapshot block search uses the unfinalized head
network.tdh.spec.bug.7.issue: Grouping changes rewrite history, and a day’s values can change after publication
network.tdh.spec.bug.7.fixed: The recompute during the day is removed (DEV-9); the carry over history is kept (DEV-10, D121)
network.tdh.spec.bug.8.issue: Link ties are ordered differently in two code paths
network.tdh.spec.bug.9.issue: Revoking one registration can unlink a pair confirmed under another collection
network.tdh.spec.bug.10.issue: Floors read at the latest state, failures dropped silently
network.tdh.spec.bug.10.fixed: Floors read at the snapshot block (DEV-6)
network.tdh.spec.bug.11.issue: Gradient and NextGen rates from current totals
network.tdh.spec.bug.12.issue: Seasons from editable metadata; a missing trait creates a phantom season
network.tdh.spec.bug.13.issue: Two different definitions of a mint
network.tdh.spec.bug.14.issue: An oversized send removes fewer copies than requested
network.tdh.spec.bug.15.issue: Uploads mix in current values for some columns

network.tdh.spec.s13.title: 13. Conformance
network.tdh.spec.s13.body: A program conforms when it reproduces every one of the 51 conformance vectors (01 to 50, and 12b) and, for a real day, the reference implementation’s output from the same inputs. The Python reference, the Rust core and program B pass all 51; the Rust core checks 976 values in them.
network.tdh.spec.decisions.title: Decisions referenced
network.tdh.spec.decisions.intro: The owner’s decisions these pages cite, in brief. The decision record itself is not yet published.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D112: Validator v1 agrees on TDH once a day, peer to peer: each validator computes TDH-v1 with the Rust core, signs the result and compares it with 6529.io.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D116: The validator code is licensed under Apache 2.0 and is published, with the ported TDH-v1 core and its conformance vectors, before the first outside operator runs it.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D118: Every validator checks each block’s events against Ethereum’s block headers, and the headers against a finalized block its own light client follows; a node that cannot complete the checks does not sign.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D119: Two separately written programs, A and B, are to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines; both are being built.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D121: One TDH formula everywhere: 6529.io, its backend and the validators compute identical TDH with the validators’ Rust core; the open deviations are settled as listed in section 11.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D125: Every validator computes TDH with two separately written implementations before it signs, and does not sign if they disagree; anyone can add the Python reference as a third.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D128: A minimal Ethereum contract records a day’s result once both programs’ proofs verify; built and tested, deployed only when the owner approves.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D130: A new validator may take the TDH history from the network’s agreement, or check all of it itself.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D131: Ownership is read at transaction boundaries: within one transaction, each wallet’s movements of each token are netted. P26 §7.1 carries the exact rule.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D132: From 16 October 2026 the Rust core and the Python reference run daily beside 6529.io’s backend and are shown side by side; 6529.io switches to the Rust result about one week later, around 23 October 2026.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.title: Evidence
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.title: Replay of 2026-10-11
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.body: From the live per-token inputs, TDH-v1 reproduces all 132,481 wallet-token bases and every wallet and identity value. From the 388,335 indexed transfers it reproduced 10,278 of 10,280 identities and 11,128 of 11,130 wallets before D131; the two others were tokens sent out and back in one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting it reproduces all 10,280 identities and 11,130 wallets. The validator’s own Ethereum ingestion later read the raw logs from each contract’s deployment, 388,447 transfers, with the history not yet fully checked: on them the Python reference with netting gives 2,061,888,816, the live total, and equals every live identity and wallet, and the second implementation agrees on every record.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.cleanRoom.body: A second Rust implementation, written from the specification and the documents it cites without opening the Python reference or the backend’s code, found 23 places where it had to guess (2 high, 11 medium, 10 low). P26 now states a rule for every one; only the state-read adapter for edition floors (F-10) stays open, and a few fixes have no vector of their own.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.comparison.bod: From independent inputs (Ethereum logs, history not yet fully checked), the Rust core was compared with 6529.io’s published files in every compared field. Before D131: 10,280 of 10,282 identities and 11,131 of 11,133 wallets equal each day; the two others were tokens sent out and back within one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting: all 10,282 identities and 11,133 wallets, with totals equal to the uploads’ (2,070,436,337 and 2,073,214,934). Ranks, the balance and set-count columns (BUG-15) and display fields are not compared.
network.tdh.spec.amended: Amended on 15 October 2026: transaction netting (D131) is in section 7.1, and the conformance vectors grew from 36 to 51.
network.tdh.spec.symbols.title: Symbols
network.tdh.spec.symbols.intro: The letters the rule uses, and where each is defined.
network.tdh.spec.symbol.M: The cycle’s boundary, N × 86,400 seconds: 00:00 UTC
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B: The snapshot block: the last finalized block before M
network.tdh.spec.symbol.T: The snapshot block’s timestamp; ages are measured to it
network.tdh.spec.symbol.days: Whole days from an acquisition time a to T
network.tdh.spec.symbol.H: The largest effective edition among eligible Memes
network.tdh.spec.symbol.G: Gradients minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.Nc: NextGen collection c’s tokens minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.net: Address w’s net movement of one token in one transaction
network.tdh.spec.symbol.raw: A token’s whole days, summed over its copies
network.tdh.spec.symbol.base: Rate × raw, rounded: a token’s TDH before the boost
network.tdh.spec.symbol.sets: Full sets: the smallest balance of any eligible Meme, when every one is held
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B64: The nearest binary64 number; it decides ties
network.tdh.spec.s3.decoding: Log selection and decoding are summarised here; the full rules, including every malformed-log case, are in P26 §3.1 and §3.2 (source to be published). The event signatures are below.
network.tdh.spec.s7.property: The rule’s property: TDH depends only on each transaction’s net movement of each token per address. Inserting, removing or reordering steps that leave every net movement unchanged changes no value (vectors 45 to 47), and the Lean model proves it for the holding stacks. Only the underflow test and the edition counts read the steps themselves (vectors 44 and 40).
network.tdh.spec.decision.legend: All settled by D121; DEV-2 amended by D131. Adopted: TDH-v1’s rule, which changed no value on the replayed cycle. Spec wins: on-chain order across transactions, netting within one. Old behavior kept: TDH-v1 keeps the backend’s behavior. Kept, not in consensus: sink records stay, and never count toward consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t1: No row, then REGISTER(a, b): pending, registered by a.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t2: Pending, then the other wallet registers back: confirmed.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t3: Confirmed, then either wallet revokes: pending again, as the other wallet’s registration.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t4: Pending, then the registering wallet revokes: no row.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t5: Confirmed, then the confirming direction registers again: still confirmed, with a newer position.
